title: Solutions
seo_title: Solutions Class 12 Chemistry Worksheet with Answers (NCERT Chapter 1)
standard_text: Types of solutions, expression of concentration of solutions of solids in liquids, solubility of gases in liquids, solid solutions, Raoult's law, colligative properties – relative lowering of vapour pressure, elevation of boiling point, depression of freezing point, osmotic pressure, determination of molecular masses using colligative properties, abnormal molecular mass, van't Hoff factor.
meta_desc: Free CBSE Class 12 Chemistry worksheets for NCERT Chapter 1 Solutions: concentration terms, Henry's law, Raoult's law, colligative properties, osmotic pressure, molar mass and the van't Hoff factor. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Colligative properties depend only on the number of solute particles.
key_sub: ΔT(b) = iK(b)m; ΔT(f) = iK(f)m; π = iCRT.
body_html:
How to think about it

Concentration may be given as mass per cent, mole fraction, molarity or molality. Henry's law says gas solubility is proportional to its partial pressure. Raoult's law gives the vapour pressure of a component as p = xp°; a non-volatile solute lowers the vapour pressure, and Δp/p° equals its mole fraction.

Colligative properties — relative lowering of vapour pressure, boiling point elevation Kbm, freezing point depression Kfm and osmotic pressure CRT — depend only on the number of particles. Electrolytes give more particles, so they are multiplied by the van't Hoff factor i.

Example

0.1 m glucose in water. ΔTf?

1.86 × 0.1

Answer: 0.186 K

Example

i for NaCl?

Na⁺ + Cl⁻

Answer: 2

Common mistakes

  • Using molarity instead of molality for ΔT.
  • Forgetting i for electrolytes.
  • Using the mass of solution instead of the solvent.

faq.a: Properties of solutions that depend only on the number of solute particles, such as osmotic pressure and freezing point depression.

faq.q: What is the van't Hoff factor?
faq.a: The ratio of the actual number of particles in solution to the number of formula units dissolved.

items.q: What is reverse osmosis used for?
items.e: Pressure greater than the osmotic pressure is applied.

items.q: 21 g of sucrose (C₁₂H₂₂O₁₁) is dissolved in water to make 100 mL of solution. What is the molarity? (molar mass 342 g mol⁻¹)
items.e: Moles = 21 ÷ 342 = 0.0614 mol; M = moles ÷ volume in L = 0.0614 ÷ 0.1 = 0.614 mol L⁻¹.

items.q: 2.5 g of sucrose (C₁₂H₂₂O₁₁) is dissolved in 500 g of water. What is the molality of the solution? (molar mass 342 g mol⁻¹)
items.e: Molality = moles of solute ÷ mass of solvent in kg = 0.00731 ÷ 0.5 = 0.0146 mol kg⁻¹.

items.q: A solution contains 1 mol of ethanol and 2.5 mol of water. What is the mole fraction of ethanol?
items.e: x = n(ethanol) ÷ (total moles) = 1 ÷ 3.5 = 0.286.

items.q: 16 g of NaOH is dissolved in 250 g of water. What is the molality of the solution? (molar mass 40 g mol⁻¹)

items.q: What are colligative properties?
